note: The states a change moves through here, each naming the ONE role that can advance it and the DOOR the next role will not take the work without. Authored: a state's meaning and its door are judgements. NOT authored: which states are occupied, which have ever been passed, and therefore which doors are shut — those are counted from the board on every build. Seven of the nine states carry a stage of the seven-stage change control declared in admin/build/gen_board.py, and a gate refuses a build where the two disagree.

states.label: Raised
states.means: A memo, a reading or a gate failure has named something that might change.
states.door: It is written down verbatim where it can be checked: a brief, a review item or an issue file. A thing said in passing has not been raised.

states.label: Planned
states.means: Which roles have a voice on this, and which are only asked for an opinion.
states.door: The split is recorded BEFORE any opinion is written. Deciding afterwards who had a voice is deciding the answer.

states.label: Mapped
states.means: What the thing actually is, counted rather than argued.
states.door: Every claim anchored to bytes or to a computation that can be re-run. A map that agrees with everyone has not been made.

states.label: Defined
states.means: The candidates, or the deliverable itself, exist.
states.door: Built only from the estate's own counted vocabulary, with what each option costs stated beside it.

states.label: Reviewed
states.means: The opinions are in, each from its role's own centre of gravity.
states.door: Every role with a voice has spoken, and each has said what it would refuse. A round of agreement is not a review.

states.label: Approved
states.means: The founder has decided. No role approves; the team proposes and the founder chooses.
states.door: The founder answers. There is no substitute, no timeout and no default, which is the point of separating proposing from choosing.

states.label: Implemented
states.means: The change is made, in the source of truth rather than in a projection of it.
states.door: Both gates green: the unit suite and the release validator. Neither is advisory.

states.label: Accepted
states.means: The founder confirms that what was built is what was approved.
states.door: The founder reads the result on the live site, not the description of it.

states.label: Shipped
states.means: Narrated, tagged, deployed, and readable by anyone.
states.door: A row in the version table saying what changed and why, and green CI. Terminal.
